subject: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 14, 2024 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)

Hi all — looping you in because Sales/CS is already asking how to message the new automation workstream, and I want us aligned before we update enablement + customer comms.

Two things to confirm:

1) What exactly is “Ready” for Dedicated capacity (net-new pools + expansions)?
   - My current draft: “Ready” means the pool has passed automated readiness gates (networking + GPU health + runtime smoke) AND perf-canary, has been registered in the control plane, and routing will advertise it.
   - “Provisioned” / “Bootstrapped” are *not* customer-facing milestones.

2) What lead time targets can we credibly commit to / state as expectations?
   - Sales wants a simple answer. CS wants language for ongoing expansions.
   - I’d like to publish “typical” + “p95” style ranges, with an explicit exceptions clause (SKUs, quotas, region, customer change windows).

Asks:
- Please reply with: (a) your proposed Ready definition (one paragraph) and (b) the lead time target ranges you’re comfortable with (separately for expansions vs net-new) and any required caveats.
- If we should avoid numbers entirely and stick to “hours to <1 business day” etc, say so.

Context:
- This is in support of the provision-to-ready automation sprint. Confluence overview + SLO proposal are linked in the thread metadata.
- Goal is to keep us from over-promising during the pilot while still giving Sales/CS something concrete.

Thanks,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Director of Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference



From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 14, 2024 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)

Agree w/ your Ready definition with one tweak: call out “Ready” is a control-plane state that gates routing.

Draft (feel free to reuse):
“Ready means the Dedicated pool has completed provisioning + imaging + bootstrap, passed automated readiness gates (GPU + networking + runtime smoke) and perf-canary, is registered with the Redwood control plane, and is eligible to receive traffic (routing will only advertise Ready capacity).”

Lead time targets (what I’m comfortable putting in enablement, not as an SLA yet):
- Expansion into an existing pool in an already-approved region/SKU: typically same day; we should message “hours” and set expectation that p95 can be within 1 business day depending on cloud quota + imaging.
- Net-new pool (new region and/or new SKU, new networking/IAM setup): usually 3–5 business days end-to-end given procurement/quota + customer change windows. The automation sprint reduces the *Redwood-controlled* portion, but doesn’t eliminate quota lead times.

Caveats I’d insist we include:
- Cloud quota / hardware availability is the #1 swing factor.
- Customer maintenance windows / approvals can push dates.
- When we’re doing heterogeneous SKUs, imaging artifacts sometimes lag in a region (we’re explicitly addressing this).

If Neha wants a single headline: “Once capacity is allocated, we aim to get it Ready within hours, not days.”

Irene

—
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 14, 2024 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)

+1 to Irene’s framing.

From an SRE perspective, I’d strongly recommend:
- Use “typical” and “target” language externally until we have 4–6 weeks of clean data.
- When we do publish a number, we should anchor it to “time from provisioning run start” (not from contract signature / PO / quota request) to avoid misinterpretation.

Ready definition (SRE-friendly):
“Ready is the point where the pool meets all automated safety checks and is explicitly marked Ready by the control plane, which is the only state that allows routing to send production traffic.”

Lead time suggestion (for enablement/FAQ):
- Expansions: “Same day in most cases (hours), with occasional 1 business day outliers.”
- Net-new: “A few business days depending on region/SKU availability and customer change windows.”

Also: please do not use “provisioned” in customer-facing comms. People hear “provisioned” and assume traffic is safe.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Director of Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 14, 2024 at 1:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)

Confirming control plane semantics:
- Only “Ready” capacity is advertised to routing.
- “Validating” is explicitly *not* usable. We had previous ambiguity here; the sprint work (ENG-2759) makes this enforcement stricter.

I’m aligned to the Ready definition as written. I’d add one line that “Ready implies rollback/fallback policies are installed” (e.g., safe defaults in helm values, telemetry wired) because it’s part of what we expect before taking traffic.

Re: lead times, I’m comfortable with Irene/Sean’s ranges.

One caution for messaging: mention we have an operator break-glass path for validation policy gates (audited). That tends to satisfy security-focused prospects, but we should be careful not to imply we’ll skip safety checks casually.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Feb 15, 2024 at 8:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated 'Ready' definition + lead time messaging (Provision-to-ready sprint)

Adding detail (in case helpful for the FAQ):

What “Ready” includes in the automation pipeline:
- Provisioned infra (Terraform apply succeeded; outputs recorded)
- Golden image applied (pinned drivers + runtime prereqs)
- Cluster bootstrap completed (k8s, base addons)
- Config validated (schema + policy checks; exceptions require break-glass + audit log)
- Readiness gates passed (GPU health incl ECC, DNS/TLS, runtime smoke)
- Perf-canary “readiness suite” passed (minimal benchmark w/ pass/fail thresholds)
- Control plane state == Ready

For lead times, I’d rather we say:
- “Typical expansion: a few hours once infra capacity is allocated”
- “Net-new: varies; usually several business days due to quotas + networking approvals”

Reason: we can control pipeline stage budgets, but cloud quotas make hard commitments risky.

Vanessa

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Engineering Manager, Fleet Automation
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — I consolidated into a one-pager + FAQ draft for Sales/CS.

Attachment/link stubs:
- Ready_State_Definition_OnePager_v0.4.pdf
- Dedicated_Readiness_and_Lead_Time_FAQ_v1.3.docx (link)

Proposed customer-facing language (pull quotes):

READY (definition):
“Dedicated capacity is considered Ready when it has passed automated safety checks (GPU + networking + runtime smoke) and a lightweight performance canary, is registered with the Redwood control plane, and is eligible to receive production traffic. Routing only sends traffic to pools marked Ready.”

LEAD TIMES (expectations):
- Expansions (existing pool / approved region & SKU): “Typically same-day (hours) once capacity is allocated; occasional cases can extend to ~1 business day due to quota or regional imaging artifacts.”
- Net-new pools: “Usually several business days end-to-end, primarily driven by region/SKU availability, quota approvals, and customer change windows. Redwood’s automated bring-up reduces the hands-on portion and provides a more predictable readiness check before traffic.”

Caveats section includes quota + maintenance windows + heterogenous SKUs.

Neha: if you’re okay, I’ll have CS Ops update macros + Sales enablement tomorrow morning and we’ll use this language in the next customer expansion comms.

Please reply with “approved” or edits by EOD tomorrow so we don’t stall.

Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Director of Product, Dedicated
